title: Spec of a local ring of a scheme is the limit of the affine open neighbourhoods of the point
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $x\in X$, $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ its local ring [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] and $g_x:\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{X,x}\to X$ the canonical morphism [lem-weil-pbc-spec-local-ring-canonical-morphism] ($\operatorname{Spec}$ as in [def-weil-affine-spectrum]). Let $N_x$ be the set of affine open subschemes $W\subseteq X$ with $x\in W$ ([def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]: $W$ is isomorphic to the spectrum of a ring), ordered by $W'\ge W$ if and only if $W'\subseteq W$; for $W'\subseteq W$ in $N_x$ let $j_{W'W}:W'\to W$ be the inclusion, an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]. Then: (1) every open subset $U\subseteq X$ with $x\in U$ contains some $W\in N_x$; in particular $N_x$ is nonempty and directed (for $W,W'\in N_x$ there is $W''\in N_x$ with $W''\subseteq W\cap W'$), and $(W,j_{W'W})$ is an inverse system of schemes over $N_x$. (2) Every $W\in N_x$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and every $j_{W'W}$ is an affine morphism ([def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], [pqf-def-affine-morphism]). (3) For every open $U\ni x$ there is a unique morphism $g_{x,U}:\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{X,x}\to U$ with $j_U\circ g_{x,U}=g_x$, $j_U:U\to X$ the inclusion, and $(\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{X,x},(g_{x,W})_{W\in N_x})$ is a limit of the inverse system $(W,j_{W'W})_{W\in N_x}$ in the category of schemes ([def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], dually): for every scheme $T$ and morphisms $t_W:T\to W$ with $j_{W'W}\circ t_{W'}=t_W$ for all $W'\subseteq W$ in $N_x$ there is exactly one morphism $t:T\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{X,x}$ with $g_{x,W}\circ t=t_W$ for all $W\in N_x$.

Hence Spec(O_{X,x}) = lim W where W runs over the affine open neighbourhoods'; the limit of affine schemes is Lemma Tag 01YW (lemma-directed-inverse-system-affine-schemes-has-limit, line 42)

proof.text: *Clause (1).* Let $U\subseteq X$ be open with $x\in U$. Since the affine opens of $X$ form a basis of the topology [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis], there is an open $W$ with $x\in W\subseteq U$ whose open subscheme is affine, i.e. $W\in N_x$. With $U=X$ this gives $N_x\ne\emptyset$; with $U=W\cap W'$ for $W,W'\in N_x$ (open, containing $x$) it gives $W''\in N_x$ with $W''\subseteq W\cap W'$, so $N_x$ is directed. For $W'\subseteq W$ in $N_x$ the inclusion $j_{W'W}$ of the open subscheme $(W',\mathcal O_X|_{W'})$ into $(W,\mathcal O_X|_W)$ is the inclusion on spaces and the identity $\mathcal O_X|_{W'}=(\mathcal O_X|_W)|_{W'}$ on sheaves, an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]; hence $j_{WW}=\mathrm{id}_W$ and $j_{W'W}\circ j_{W''W'}=j_{W''W}$ for $W''\subseteq W'\subseteq W$ (both sides are the inclusion of the same open subscheme), so $(W,j_{W'W})_{W\in N_x}$ is an inverse system of schemes over $N_x$.

proof.text: *Clause (2).* Every $W\in N_x$ is an affine scheme, hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. For $W'\subseteq W$ in $N_x$, $j_{W'W}:W'\to W$ is a morphism between affine schemes, hence an affine morphism [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-affine-schemes-affine].

proof.text: *The morphisms $g_{x,U}$ (first part of clause (3)).* Let $U\ni x$ be open. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-local-ring-canonical-morphism] (1) the image of $g_x$ is the set of generalizations of $x$, which lies in every open containing $x$, so $g_x(\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{X,x})\subseteq U$. By [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme] there is a unique morphism $g_{x,U}:\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{X,x}\to U$ with $j_U\circ g_{x,U}=g_x$. For $W'\subseteq W$ in $N_x$ we have $j_W\circ(j_{W'W}\circ g_{x,W'})=j_{W'}\circ g_{x,W'}=g_x$ (step 1: $j_W\circ j_{W'W}=j_{W'}$, both being the inclusion of $W'$ in $X$), so the uniqueness just used gives $j_{W'W}\circ g_{x,W'}=g_{x,W}$: $(\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{X,x},(g_{x,W})_{W\in N_x})$ is a cone over the inverse system of clause (1).

proof.text: *$\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is the colimit of the rings $\mathcal O_X(W)$, $W\in N_x$.* Put $R_W=\mathcal O_X(W)$, let $\rho_{W'W}:R_W\to R_{W'}$ be the restriction for $W'\subseteq W$ in $N_x$ and $\gamma_W:R_W\to\mathcal O_{X,x}$, $r\mapsto r_x$, the germ map [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk], a ring homomorphism with $\gamma_{W'}\circ\rho_{W'W}=\gamma_W$ (the germ of a restriction is the germ). So $(R_W,\rho)$ is a directed system of commutative rings over the directed set $N_x$ (step 1) and $(\mathcal O_{X,x},\gamma_W)$ a cocone on it. It is a colimit in the category of commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]: let $(M,\mu_W)$ be a cocone of ring homomorphisms. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-stalk-germs-on-basis] to the presheaf of rings $\mathcal O_X$ and the basis $\mathcal B$ of affine opens [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis]; its members containing $x$ are the elements of $N_x$. By (i) every element of $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is $\gamma_W(s)$ for some $W\in N_x$, $s\in R_W$; define $u(\gamma_W(s))=\mu_W(s)$. This is well defined: if $\gamma_W(s)=\gamma_{W'}(t)$, (ii) gives $W''\in N_x$, $W''\subseteq W\cap W'$, with $\rho_{W''W}(s)=\rho_{W''W'}(t)$, so $\mu_W(s)=\mu_{W''}(\rho_{W''W}(s))=\mu_{W''}(\rho_{W''W'}(t))=\mu_{W'}(t)$. It is a ring homomorphism: two elements $\gamma_W(s),\gamma_{W'}(t)$ are $\gamma_{W''}(\rho_{W''W}(s)),\gamma_{W''}(\rho_{W''W'}(t))$ for a $W''\in N_x$ below $W$ and $W'$ (step 1), and $\gamma_{W''}$, $\mu_{W''}$ are ring homomorphisms; $u(1)=\mu_W(1)=1$. By construction $u\circ\gamma_W=\mu_W$, and $u$ is the only such map since the $\gamma_W(s)$ exhaust $\mathcal O_{X,x}$.

proof.text: *Spec of the colimit.* By step 4 and [lem-weil-pbc-spec-colimit-limit] (applied to the directed system $(R_W,\rho_{W'W})$ over $N_x$ with colimit $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ and coprojections $\gamma_W$), $\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{X,x}$ with the morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}\gamma_W:\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{X,x}\to\operatorname{Spec}R_W$ is a limit of the inverse system $(\operatorname{Spec}R_W,\operatorname{Spec}\rho_{W'W})_{W\in N_x}$ in the category of schemes [def-weil-affine-spectrum].

source.place: Lemma Tag 01YW (lemma-directed-inverse-system-affine-schemes-has-limit, line 42) and its proof (line 52-56); Lemma Tag 0GWT (lemma-morphism-glueing-near-closed-point, line 1530), proof, line 1561-1564: 'Hence Spec(O_{X,x}) = lim W'

proof.text: *From $\operatorname{Spec}R_W$ to $W$.* For $W\in N_x$ let $\iota_W:\operatorname{Spec}R_W\to X$ be the canonical open immersion with image $W$ of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-spec-points], the inverse of the isomorphism $W\cong\operatorname{Spec}R_W$ followed by $j_W$; so $\iota_W=j_W\circ\kappa_W$ with $\kappa_W:\operatorname{Spec}R_W\to W$ an isomorphism of schemes. For $W'\subseteq W$ in $N_x$, [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-inclusion-spec-map] gives $\iota_W\circ\operatorname{Spec}\rho_{W'W}=\iota_{W'}$, i.e. $j_W\circ\kappa_W\circ\operatorname{Spec}\rho_{W'W}=j_{W'}\circ\kappa_{W'}=j_W\circ j_{W'W}\circ\kappa_{W'}$, and since the open immersion $j_W$ is a monomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-monomorphism], $\kappa_W\circ\operatorname{Spec}\rho_{W'W}=j_{W'W}\circ\kappa_{W'}$. Thus the $\kappa_W$ form an isomorphism of inverse systems $(\operatorname{Spec}R_W,\operatorname{Spec}\rho)\to(W,j)$ over $N_x$. Composing with it carries limit cones to limit cones: for a scheme $T$, families $(t_W:T\to W)$ compatible with the $j$ correspond bijectively to families $(\kappa_W^{-1}\circ t_W)$ compatible with the $\operatorname{Spec}\rho$, by the displayed identity. Hence, by step 5, $\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{X,x}$ with the morphisms $\kappa_W\circ\operatorname{Spec}\gamma_W$ is a limit of $(W,j_{W'W})_{W\in N_x}$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0GWT (lemma-morphism-glueing-near-closed-point, line 1530), proof, line 1561-1564: 'Spec(O_{X,x}) = lim W' (W identified with Spec O_W(W))

proof.text: *The projections are the $g_{x,W}$; conclusion.* Let $W\in N_x$ and let $\mathfrak p\subset R_W$ be the prime corresponding to $x$. By the description of the canonical morphism in [lem-weil-pbc-spec-local-ring-canonical-morphism] for the affine open $V=W\cong\operatorname{Spec}R_W$ (the identification being $\iota_W$), $g_x=\iota_W\circ\operatorname{Spec}(\varphi)$, where $\varphi:R_W\to(R_W)_{\mathfrak p}\cong\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is the localization map followed by the natural isomorphism $r/s\mapsto r_xs_x^{-1}$ [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization] (c); so $\varphi(r)=r_x=\gamma_W(r)$, i.e. $\varphi=\gamma_W$. Hence $g_x=j_W\circ(\kappa_W\circ\operatorname{Spec}\gamma_W)$, and the uniqueness of step 3 gives $g_{x,W}=\kappa_W\circ\operatorname{Spec}\gamma_W$. By step 6, $(\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{X,x},(g_{x,W})_{W\in N_x})$ is a limit of $(W,j_{W'W})$, which, by the definition of a limit (dual of [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]), is the property stated in clause (3): for compatible $t_W:T\to W$ there is exactly one $t:T\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathcal O_{X,x}$ with $g_{x,W}\circ t=t_W$ for all $W\in N_x$.
